nodes.label: §9 Public Client API (Frozen Contract)
nodes.rationale: Frozen first because Clementine and every other product builds against activate/validate/deactivate/heartbeat/usage shapes; drift would break shipped clients with no migration path.

nodes.label: The license object (key,status,kind,plan,product,expires_at)
nodes.rationale: plan is a free-form vendor label and display only; never an authorization input. expires_at is advisory for subscription and enforced only for trial, so a client never enforces on its own clock.

nodes.label: POST /v1/validate
nodes.rationale: A known key always returns 200, including a disabled one, so the client sees the definitive revocation signal rather than an inconclusive error.

nodes.label: POST /v1/heartbeat (floating lease renew)
nodes.rationale: An expired lease frees the seat automatically so a crashed client never permanently consumes a floating seat; null lease_expires_at lets a client tell 'lease held' from 're-activate'.

nodes.label: POST /v1/keyset
nodes.rationale: POST not GET because the key is the credential and a URL lands in access logs and history; resolves signing keys from the key so an app needs no product slug.

nodes.label: POST /v1/usage/increment
nodes.rationale: Bound to a live seat; unknown and deactivated instances answer identically so the endpoint never confirms an instance id existed. A lapsed floating lease is deliberately not rejected.

nodes.label: Lemon Squeezy compatibility routes /v1/licenses/*
nodes.rationale: An alias serializer over the same handlers, not a second implementation, so a base-URL swap migrates an LS client; these routes omit the ok envelope to reproduce the LS shape exactly.

nodes.label: Unknown key is 404, never disabled
nodes.rationale: A data gap or not-yet-imported key must never read as revocation, or an offline machine would lock out on its next revalidation.

nodes.label: Offline-tolerant by contract
nodes.rationale: A network failure or inconclusive answer never locks a user out; only an explicit disabled signal revokes access.

nodes.label: The key is the credential
nodes.rationale: Public endpoints authenticate by the key itself so no service secret ships in a client binary; Cool Beans holds the Stripe/PayPal/email secrets.

nodes.label: Key generation and normalization
nodes.rationale: Ambiguity-free alphabet plus rejection sampling for ~78 bits of entropy, so key validity is not a useful enumeration oracle; one shared normalizer rejects malformed keys before touching storage.

nodes.label: Ed25519 signed offline token
nodes.rationale: A signed expires_at in the past ends access offline too, because honouring our own credential is not guessing from a network failure; that is what makes subscription revocation reach a dark machine.

nodes.label: OFFLINE_TOKEN_BUFFER_DAYS renewal buffer
nodes.rationale: The token's date is the server's choice with a buffer so a subscriber who renews while offline has room to reconnect; never applied to trials or perpetual licences.

nodes.label: Offline activation for air-gapped machines
nodes.rationale: Blob carries a signed fingerprint claim or the check would be circular on instance_id; refused for floating products because a lapsing lease would let one seat mint unbounded activations.

nodes.label: @coolbeans/sdk one-call open()
nodes.rationale: Everything an app used to decide (activate vs validate, online vs cached, what inconclusive means) was a way to lock out a paying customer, so the SDK decides all of it.

nodes.label: AccessState verdict (allow/deny discriminated union)
nodes.rationale: A union rather than a boolean because 'never established an entitlement' and 'you were revoked' are different screens; a boolean loses that.

nodes.label: Signed entitlements (flat map of scalars)
nodes.rationale: A flat signed capability map ships but entitlement graphs do not; signed by us, unlike a plan label a vendor typed, which is why it is the only safe thing to gate on.

nodes.label: Activation limit and live-seat count
nodes.rationale: Live seats are activations where deactivated_at IS NULL; reactivating the same device reuses its instance rather than burning a seat.

nodes.label: Atomic limit enforcement in the database
nodes.rationale: Single guarded statements, never read-then-write, so two concurrent requests can never both pass a limit check; each path gets a dedicated race test.
nodes.norm_label: atomic limit enforcement in the database

nodes.label: Trial licence kind
nodes.rationale: The one kind where expires_at is enforced, lazily at validate/verify, and the one kind with no offline TTL grace, or a blocked endpoint would be an unlimited trial.

nodes.label: Perpetual licence kind
nodes.rationale: No expires_at, so subscription events never touch it; it dies only on refund or chargeback.

nodes.label: Subscription licence kind
nodes.rationale: expires_at tracks the Stripe period end and stays advisory client-side; lapse enforcement is customer.subscription.deleted, not a client date check.

nodes.label: License grant (one Stripe price to one product)
nodes.rationale: Seats and entitlements are snapshotted at issuance so re-pricing never changes what somebody already bought, which is what lets one product sell Basic and Pro; grants are retired, never deleted, to keep provenance.
nodes.norm_label: license grant (one stripe price to one product)

nodes.label: Stripe connection (self_host_default | cloud_connect)
nodes.rationale: The webhook signing secret lives on the connection, not the product, so one self-host instance has exactly one Stripe webhook endpoint however many products it runs.

nodes.label: POST /v1/stripe/webhook event handling
nodes.rationale: Only a full refund disables; dispute.created is handled because a lost chargeback emits no charge.refunded; renewal refunds resolve via invoice→subscription since the stored payment intent will not match.

nodes.label: Two-layer webhook idempotency
nodes.rationale: provider_events dedupes a redelivered event id and purchases.provider_checkout_id UNIQUE stops double issuance even across the success-page race; a failed key email returns 500 with email_sent_at NULL so only the email retries.

nodes.label: Key delivery (success page + email)
nodes.rationale: Both channels are fed by one idempotent issuance path, so whichever of webhook or success page runs first issues and the other reads. No race, no check-back-later state.

nodes.label: Customer portal
nodes.rationale: Self-service seat deactivation is what keeps support out of the seat-management loop.

nodes.label: Admin API, dashboard and CLI
nodes.rationale: Slug and key prefix are immutable after creation because issued keys embed the prefix and clients match on the slug.

nodes.label: Per-product signing keys with rotation
nodes.rationale: Private half encrypted at rest, public half embedded in apps, multiple active public keys so rotation needs no app release.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant accounts model
nodes.rationale: An instance is in cloud mode exactly when platform billing is configured, so it can never enforce a limit nobody has a way to pay to lift; self-host stays single-account and unlimited through the same code path.

nodes.label: Pricing: self-host free, Cloud Free, Cloud Pro $99/yr flat
nodes.rationale: Marginal cost per validate is about one indexed read, so nothing needs to meter on the thing that grows with a customer's success; caps are enforced on creation only and never disable or delete.
nodes.norm_label: pricing: self-host free, cloud free, cloud pro $99/yr flat

nodes.label: The frozen contract (architecture view)
nodes.rationale: Any change to the §9 shapes needs a very good reason and a migration story for every shipped client.

nodes.label: contract/access-states.json shared fixtures
nodes.rationale: The second frozen thing: both SDKs run every case, so neither can change who keeps working without failing a test. Editing it is editing the product's behaviour.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL everywhere (one dialect)
nodes.rationale: The SQLite port was a rewrite of the atomic-enforcement paths, not a config switch; PGlite in tests is real Postgres through the same Database type with no casts.

nodes.label: Atomicity needs locks, not just guarded statements
nodes.rationale: Under MVCC every contender evaluates a COUNT guard against its own snapshot: a 3-seat cap admitted 12 contenders. Seats and lease revival serialise on the licence row, product caps on the accounts row; heartbeat and unlimited plans deliberately take no lock.
nodes.norm_label: atomicity needs locks, not just guarded statements

nodes.label: Never read a driver rowcount
nodes.rationale: postgres-js has no result.changes and undefined === 0 is false, so a missed conversion silently stops enforcing a cap with nothing in any log; applied()/affected() plus a source-scan test ban every count-field spelling.

nodes.label: withTx transaction binding
nodes.rationale: A helper handed the outer deps writes outside the transaction, so a rolled-back issuance leaves a purchase whose UNIQUE checkout id blocks every provider retry forever.

nodes.label: Webhook claim fence token
nodes.rationale: The fence is minted by the claim statement itself via RETURNING and never re-read, which is the gap that would hand an elder claimant its successor's fence.

nodes.label: Outbox drain with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.norm_label: outbox drain with for update skip locked

nodes.label: ISO-8601 string dates compared lexicographically
nodes.rationale: now()::text yields a space instead of T and ' ' < 'T', which alone would make the retention prune delete finished events immediately.

nodes.label: Migrations run in exactly one place
nodes.rationale: N replicas plus a worker plus a deploy Job would race DDL, so boot runs assertSchemaCurrent and refuses to serve a schema the build was not made for.
nodes.norm_label: migrations run in exactly one place

nodes.label: Retention policy for provider_events and audit_log
nodes.rationale: provider_events prunes at 30 days, far outside Stripe's ~3 day retry window, and only finished rows go because deleting a processing row would let the same event run twice; audit_log is never pruned automatically.
nodes.norm_label: retention policy for provider_events and audit_log

nodes.label: Tenancy decisions (accounts row is the tenant)
nodes.rationale: Grants and connections are tenant-locked by composite foreign key so a grant crossing tenants is impossible at the database layer; slug and key_prefix stay globally unique because both appear in public URLs.
nodes.norm_label: tenancy decisions (accounts row is the tenant)

nodes.label: Cross-account is 404, never 403
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the slug or id exists in somebody else's account; requireProduct is the one place that decides it, and a route-inventory test fails when a new /admin route lacks a tenancy assertion.

nodes.label: The public /v1 surface is never account-scoped
nodes.rationale: An account join adds a way for a valid key to stop working and buys nothing against someone who already holds the key.
nodes.norm_label: the public /v1 surface is never account-scoped

nodes.label: Account 1 always exists
nodes.rationale: Grandfathered to pro so an existing install does not wake up capped and a self-hoster gets a working instance with no signup ceremony.

nodes.label: Platform billing as the single cloud-mode flag
nodes.rationale: One flag rather than two means an instance can never enforce a limit nobody has a way to pay to lift.
nodes.norm_label: platform billing as the single cloud-mode flag

nodes.label: BILLING_* separate from STRIPE_* (four isolation layers)
nodes.rationale: Distinct URL, distinct signing secret, distinct gateway and a strict price filter, plus a reverse guard so a product can never be configured onto the Pro price; config refuses to start in production if the keys match.
nodes.norm_label: billing_* separate from stripe_* (four isolation layers)

nodes.label: gb_app metadata stamp for shared-account webhook routing
nodes.rationale: Stripe fans every subscribed event to every endpoint on the account, so siblings bounce with 200 before claiming; absence of the stamp must never bounce because dashboard-created objects carry none, and the price filter stays the authority on money.
nodes.norm_label: gb_app metadata stamp for shared-account webhook routing

nodes.label: Limits hard at a keyboard, soft where money has moved
nodes.rationale: Webhook-driven issuance never refuses because a Free customer's buyer has just paid them; we issue, log, audit and stamp over_limit_since instead of breaking their business to collect an upgrade fee.
nodes.norm_label: limits hard at a keyboard, soft where money has moved

nodes.label: Bespoke email magic-code console auth
nodes.rationale: Better Auth's organization support would have meant importing its user/session tables, migrating live sessions and rewriting the magic-code flow, where tenancy actually needed one integer column on three tables.

nodes.label: Ed25519 offline tokens, never HMAC
nodes.rationale: A symmetric secret shipped inside a desktop binary is extractable and forgeable; an embedded public key is not. TTL is configurable because it is a revocation-latency SLA.

nodes.label: Cool Beans design system (v2)
nodes.rationale: Clean, white and calm, a tool you leave open all day; one loud lime accent used sparingly, keys and ids always monospace because that is the product's signature.

nodes.label: Color tokens (warm ink on white, lime accent)
nodes.norm_label: color tokens (warm ink on white, lime accent)

nodes.label: Type scale (Instrument Sans + IBM Plex Mono)
nodes.norm_label: type scale (instrument sans + ibm plex mono)

nodes.label: Component vocabulary (status pill, kind, meters, dialogs)
nodes.norm_label: component vocabulary (status pill, kind, meters, dialogs)

nodes.label: Voice (plain, warm, a little proud)
nodes.rationale: Microcopy explains the contract in one breath: 'No password. No account. The key is the credential.' Never scolds, never yells.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery contract
nodes.rationale: A dead receiver never slows or fails issuance, so delivery is asynchronous; handlers must be idempotent on (event.type, license.key, event.created_at).

nodes.label: Never gate a feature on webhook arrival
nodes.rationale: The webhook stream is for your own systems (CRM, analytics, Slack); the application keeps using the client SDK contract.
nodes.norm_label: never gate a feature on webhook arrival

nodes.label: PRD validation matrix
nodes.rationale: Exact test counts are left to the runner so the document cannot drift every time coverage grows.

nodes.label: §9 example vs §10 key length discrepancy
nodes.rationale: The build follows §10's normative 16 chars, which preserves the 'prefix plus 16 alphanumerics' LS-compat claim; the §9 example showing 12 is read as illustrative.

nodes.label: Commercial journey scripts
nodes.rationale: The vitest suites prove the internals; these prove what customers pay for, with real HMAC signatures rather than a bypass, because a suite that skipped signatures missed connect blanking a stored webhook secret.

nodes.label: Our own Stripe stand-in, not stripe-mock
nodes.rationale: The official mock serves canned fixtures, so a session's line items would never carry the configured price id, which is exactly the assertion that catches issuance resolving to the wrong product.
nodes.norm_label: our own stripe stand-in, not stripe-mock

nodes.label: Provider CLI webhook checks
nodes.rationale: Synthesized payloads prove our handling but not that real provider payloads still match it, so the script asserts a key was actually issued rather than a 200.

nodes.label: EMAIL_PROVIDER=console for local work
nodes.rationale: Refused under NODE_ENV=production, because an instance that quietly logs key emails instead of sending them looks healthy while every buyer waits forever.

nodes.label: The one rule: branch on state.decision and nothing else
nodes.rationale: Every lockout seen came from an app second-guessing open(): comparing dates, inspecting license.status, or deciding what a failed request meant.
nodes.norm_label: the one rule: branch on state.decision and nothing else

nodes.label: The verdict and its reason codes
nodes.norm_label: the verdict and its reason codes

nodes.label: Gate features on state.entitlements only
nodes.rationale: if (plan === 'Pro') breaks the day somebody renames a tier; entitlements are server-authored and signed into the token.

nodes.label: Per-host durable storage table
nodes.rationale: The only thing that changes between hosts is where the device identity lives, because that is what decides whether a restart burns another seat.

nodes.label: Docs: HTTP API
nodes.rationale: Documented for languages without an SDK, with the warning that wiring it by hand means re-deciding everything open() decides, which is where lockouts come from.

nodes.label: Three rules you cannot get wrong
nodes.rationale: Unknown key is 404 never disabled; only explicit disabled revokes; the licence key is the only credential.
nodes.norm_label: three rules you cannot get wrong

nodes.label: Customer portal endpoints (lookup, recover, billing-session)
nodes.rationale: Recovery emails keys and never returns them: an email address is not a credential, and a byte-identical answer means it cannot probe who bought what.

nodes.label: The three offline states (valid / grace / expired)
nodes.rationale: grace is the one people get wrong: it means 'we have not been able to check for a while', which happens on a plane, so unlock and do not put a modal in front of it.
nodes.norm_label: the three offline states (valid / grace / expired)

nodes.label: The offline cutoff (three rules)
nodes.rationale: Network failure never locks out; a signed expires_at in the past ends access for every tier; trials get no grace at all.

nodes.label: Clock rollback floor
nodes.rationale: A clock that appears to have moved backwards is distrusted, never punished: the verdict stays allow with reason clock_rollback, so a dead CMOS battery or a fresh VM keeps working.

nodes.label: Embedded public keys are the trust anchor
nodes.rationale: A machine that has never been online still has something to check a signature against, and on a notarised app tampering with the bundle breaks the code signature; fetched keys never displace embedded ones.
nodes.norm_label: embedded public keys are the trust anchor

nodes.label: Docs: licence grants
nodes.rationale: Kind is inferred from the price and a stated wrong intent is refused rather than silently corrected, because it usually means the wrong price id was pasted.

nodes.label: Unfulfilled payment one-click rescue
nodes.rationale: A paid checkout matching no grant is recorded rather than lost or silently ignored; the rescue runs the webhook's own path so a redelivery racing it still issues exactly one key.

nodes.label: Webhook endpoint admin API (register, rotate, deliveries)
nodes.norm_label: webhook endpoint admin api (register, rotate, deliveries)

nodes.label: The three Stripe namespaces
nodes.rationale: Three separate *STRIPE* namespaces are three different Stripe accounts doing three different jobs; sharing one puts both flows on a single event stream where a Pro purchase can be mistaken for a product sale.

nodes.label: STRIPE_*: the vendor selling their software
nodes.norm_label: stripe_*: the vendor selling their software

nodes.label: BILLING_STRIPE_*: us charging for hosted Cool Beans
nodes.rationale: Setting BILLING_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is what puts the instance in cloud mode: plan limits apply and public signup opens. Blank means unlimited, which is what self-host is.
nodes.norm_label: billing_stripe_*: us charging for hosted cool beans

nodes.label: CONNECT_STRIPE_*: Stripe Connect for cloud multi-vendor
nodes.rationale: All vendor events arrive on one platform endpoint keyed by the signed event.account; without CONNECT_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in production no cloud vendor is ever paid.
nodes.norm_label: connect_stripe_*: stripe connect for cloud multi-vendor

nodes.label: Offline token env reference (TTL, buffer, activation TTL)
nodes.norm_label: offline token env reference (ttl, buffer, activation ttl)

nodes.label: ADMIN_TOKEN is unset in cloud on purpose
nodes.rationale: It is a global bypass with no account behind it, which has no place in a multi-tenant instance.
nodes.norm_label: admin_token is unset in cloud on purpose

nodes.label: No key import: parity is at the API level
nodes.rationale: An LS-issued key answers 404 unknown_key, which is inconclusive to an offline-tolerant client and never a lockout, but it also never validates, so migration means issuing fresh keys.
nodes.norm_label: no key import: parity is at the api level

nodes.label: What open() does for you
nodes.rationale: Refreshes at a third of the token's lifetime, jittered so installs do not stampede one server; holds a floating seat off the server's own lease window; timers are unref'd so a CLI still exits.

nodes.label: Durable storage required outside the browser
nodes.rationale: In-memory storage mints a new device id every launch, so a node-locked licence is spent in a handful of restarts on a customer who paid; the SDK throws storage_required instead.
nodes.norm_label: durable storage required outside the browser

nodes.label: When you need the product slug
nodes.rationale: Without a slug the first licence an install activates binds the app, and that first key is the one nobody checked, so a licence for your other product could unlock this one on a fresh install.
nodes.norm_label: when you need the product slug

nodes.label: SDK anti-patterns
nodes.rationale: Do not check on every feature use, do not act abruptly on a failure, do not reach for verify/verifyOffline, do not build a seat policy: every lockout bug came from one of these.

nodes.label: Hardware-derived device identity (IOPlatformUUID / identifierForVendor)
nodes.rationale: A reinstall or backup restore does not quietly burn another seat, which is a real failure mode with a random-UUID approach.

nodes.label: Keychain storage and iCloud sync choice
nodes.rationale: Sync on means 'it already works on my laptop'; off means each machine takes its own seat. A custom storage's set must return false on failure or the app looks activated until it quits, then takes another seat every launch.
nodes.norm_label: keychain storage and icloud sync choice

nodes.label: LicenseGate (testable SwiftUI wrapper)
nodes.rationale: All decisions live in plain Swift covered by tests and the SwiftUI file is presentation only, because logic that lives in a view is logic nobody can test.

nodes.label: beans key issue
nodes.rationale: --seats and --until are parsed before the request so a typo is caught locally rather than reaching the server as a confusing complaint.

nodes.label: beans stripe connect
nodes.rationale: Registers the connection's webhook endpoint and stores the signing secret; registration is its whole job, prices are mapped separately with grants.
